entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. For questions about an existing order or to make a return, please press one.
[Beep]
Thanks for calling VeloFit Customer Support, my name is Alex. How can I help you today?
Hi, I need to start a return for an order. It's for a pair of cycling shoes.
I can certainly help with that. Do you have the order number handy?
Yeah, it's VF-90210-B. The Pulse Carbon shoes.
Okay, let me pull that up... I see the order was delivered 16 days ago. Can I ask the reason for the return?
They just don't fit right. I took them on one ride and they created a terrible hot spot on my foot.
I see. And just to confirm, you did ride with them outdoors?
Yes. How else would I know they don't work? I **installed** the cleats and went for a 20-mile ride.

I understand, but unfortunately, that's where we run into an issue with the return policy. Once an item has been used, we're unable to accept it as a return. When cleats are **mounted** to the sole, it always leaves scuffs and **cleat marks** that prevent us from reselling the item.
Are you serious? That's ridiculous. It was one ride! The shoes are practically brand new. This is an insane policy.

I do understand the frustration. Our policy is consistent for all used gear. It's similar to tires – once they're put on a wheel and ridden, we can't take them back because they'll come back as **dirty tires**, even if they're perfectly fine.
Look, I'm not returning tires. I'm returning expensive shoes that don't fit. I'm a VIP member here; I've spent thousands of dollars with VeloFit. You need to make an exception for me.

I do see your VIP status in the system, and we truly appreciate your loyalty. However, the policy regarding the physical condition of returned items is strict, and it's one I'm not able to override. I cannot accept a return on any item that shows clear signs of use.
So you're just telling me I'm stuck with $150 shoes I can't wear? This is how you treat your best customers? By hiding behind some fine-print policy?

I genuinely wish there was more I could do about the shoes themselves. What I can offer, as a gesture of goodwill for the inconvenience and as a thank you for being a VIP member, is a $25 store credit. You could use it towards a different pair or any other gear.
A $25 credit? Are you kidding me? That's an insult. That doesn't even cover the sales tax on my last order. No, that's not a solution.
I'm sorry you feel that way. It's the maximum I'm authorized to provide in this situation.
This is unbelievable. You haven't helped me at all. You've just lost a customer for life. I'm done.
Sir, I understand you're upset, but— hello? ...Hello?
